AgroDC AI: Agricultural Intelligence using AI, Satellite Monitoring & Harvest Prediction

The AgroDC AI is an intelligent agriculture platform that leverages AI to provide agricultural intelligence. The AgroDC AI operates using hardware which allows to collect and process data when the internet connection is down. AgroDC AI also leverages the meteorology and imagery data from NASA Satellites to aid farming decision-making and to sustain global hunger challenges.

AgroDC AI – AI-Powered Agricultural Intelligence, Satellite Monitoring & Harvest Prediction

1. What does AgroDC AI do?

AgroDC AI is an integrated agricultural intelligence platform designed to connect ground-level farm conditions with large-scale satellite observations. It combines IoT-based environmental monitoring, weather datasets, artificial intelligence and NASA Earth observation data to help farmers, governments and food-grain management organisations make informed agricultural decisions.

The project consists of two interconnected models:

Model 1 – Real-Time IoT Agricultural Monitoring and Risk Analysis

This model uses an ESP32-based hardware system connected to multiple agricultural sensors, including:

  • Soil moisture sensor to measure the water content of soil.
  • DHT11 sensor to monitor environmental temperature and humidity.
  • Rain sensor to detect rainfall conditions.

The ESP32 collects environmental readings directly from the agricultural environment. The hardware is designed for offline-capable operation, allowing sensor measurements to be collected without requiring continuous internet connectivity. When network connectivity is available, the readings can be transmitted to the cloud for further processing and visualisation.

The collected information is integrated with relevant weather datasets, including rainfall, temperature and humidity observations. AI-based analytical methods can use these combined datasets to identify potential water stress, abnormal environmental conditions and agricultural risks.

The system presents sensor readings, historical trends, risk assessments and actionable recommendations through a web-based dashboard.

Model 2 – Satellite-Based Crop Intelligence and Harvest Estimation

This model expands agricultural monitoring beyond individual sensor installations by combining satellite imagery, NASA Earth observation datasets, weather information and ground-level sensor readings.

Its main functions include:

  • Agricultural Area Estimation: Analyse satellite imagery to identify agricultural land and estimate the area under cultivation.
  • Crop Health Assessment: Use vegetation indices and satellite observations to understand crop conditions and identify potentially unhealthy regions.
  • Environmental Analysis: Combine historical and current weather information with satellite observations to understand environmental influences on crop growth.
  • Harvest Prediction: Estimate potential agricultural production using farm area, crop health indicators, environmental conditions and available historical agricultural information.
  • Agricultural Risk Identification: Identify regions potentially affected by insufficient rainfall, abnormal vegetation conditions or environmental stress.

The model aims to generate approximate harvest estimates rather than guaranteed production figures. Its accuracy can improve as more ground-level measurements, historical yield records and crop-specific information become available.

2. NASA Data and Weather Integration

An important part of AgroDC AI is the integration of Earth observation and environmental datasets.

Potential NASA data sources include:

  • NASA POWER – Meteorological and solar data, including temperature and other environmental parameters.
  • NASA GPM – Global precipitation observations for rainfall analysis.
  • NASA MODIS – Satellite observations useful for vegetation monitoring and crop-health analysis.
  • NASA Earthdata – Access to relevant Earth observation datasets and satellite products.

These datasets can be combined with locally collected ESP32 sensor readings to provide a more comprehensive understanding of agricultural conditions.

3. Technologies, Hardware and Software Used

Hardware:

  • ESP32-WROOM-32 microcontroller.
  • Soil moisture sensor.
  • DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor.
  • Rain detection sensor.

Software and development technologies:

  • Arduino IDE and Embedded C/C++ for ESP32 programming.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web dashboard.
  • Supabase for database management and cloud data storage.
  • Supabase Edge Functions for receiving and processing sensor data.
  • Netlify for web application hosting.
  • AI and machine learning techniques for agricultural risk analysis, crop-health assessment and yield estimation.

4. How Does the Project Benefit Users?

For farmers:

  • Better understanding of soil and environmental conditions.
  • Early identification of potential water stress.
  • Improved irrigation and resource-management decisions.
  • Access to agricultural insights through a digital dashboard.

For governments and agricultural departments:

  • Regional agricultural monitoring.
  • Approximate production estimation.
  • Identification of potentially vulnerable agricultural regions.
  • Better support for agricultural planning and food-security policies.

For FCI and equivalent food-grain organisations worldwide:

  • Support for regional crop-production estimation.
  • Improved procurement and storage planning.
  • Better anticipation of potential grain surpluses and shortages.
  • Additional information for national food-security management.

AgroDC AI is intended to be a decision-support system, complementing rather than replacing official agricultural surveys, field inspections and procurement records.

5. What Makes AgroDC AI Creative and Innovative?

The key innovation is the integration of two different perspectives on agriculture:

  1. Ground-level observations collected directly from physical IoT sensors.
  2. Large-scale agricultural observations obtained through satellite imagery and Earth observation datasets.

Traditional sensor-based systems generally monitor only the locations where hardware is installed, while satellite-based monitoring provides a broader geographical perspective but may lack detailed local environmental measurements.

AgroDC AI aims to bridge this gap by combining both sources of information.

This creates an opportunity to move from individual farm monitoring towards regional agricultural intelligence and large-scale food-security planning.

6. Intended Impact

Our long-term vision is to develop AgroDC AI into a scalable agricultural intelligence platform that can serve different agricultural environments and countries.

By connecting individual farmers with regional and national agricultural monitoring systems, the project aims to contribute to:

  • More efficient agricultural resource management.
  • Improved awareness of crop-health conditions.
  • Better agricultural production forecasting.
  • More informed food-grain procurement and storage planning.
  • Greater preparedness for environmental and climate-related agricultural risks.
  • Improved food-security decision-making across countries.

Ultimately, AgroDC AI aims to transform agricultural data into practical intelligence, connecting farmers, satellite observations and institutional decision-makers through a unified AI-powered platform.
